report: Mrs. Taylor experienced significant confusion this morning, repeatedly asking where she was. She also complained of back pain and required two staff members to assist with transferring her from the bed to the wheelchair. Nutritious breakfast eaten well, required encouragement to drink ensure for hydration.

Mr. Johnson displayed restlessness throughout the night, frequently getting up and attempting to wander the hallways. He reported tightness of breath in the early hours and needed support to realign in bed multiple times. He interacted briefly with a visitor but seemed disconnected.

Ms. Roberts showed no interest in social activities today and remained isolated in her room. She mentioned having nausea after breakfast and needed a full assist for showering and dressing. Her family discussed their concerns about her reduced appetite and requested modifications to her care plan.

Mr. Davis had an episode of severe back pain this afternoon and was unwilling to engage in physiotherapy exercises. He experienced irritation from long nails which required trimming. He struggled with choking while eating lunch and needed help using adapted cutlery.

Mrs. Thompson developed a pressure ulcer on her right heel, leading to discomfort and agitation. She was seen by the GP, who updated her medication. Despite encouragement, she ate very little dinner. Kept hydrated as monitored. Transferred safely using the lift but appeared visibly tired.
Resident A required assistance with brushing teeth and had minimal appetite. Encouragement needed to prevent choking during meals. Showed signs of restlessness at night, often wandering the halls.
Resident B showed redness and itching on the skin, with a minor medical complaint about shortness of breath. Needed full help with eating and required adapted cutlery. Confusion present but subtle.

Resident C experienced back pain and nausea. Nails observed to be too long, and frequent incontinence care required. Limited interaction with fellow residents, but responded positively to family phone calls.
Resident D declined visitors and appeared apathetic. Necessary to manually reposition frequently due to lying crookedly in bed. Showed signs of peeling skin and minor pressure ulcers.

Resident E requested additional palliative care discussions due to persistent tightness of breath. Dependent on a wheelchair and had a recent fall incident. Needed encouragement to maintain hydration lists.

Resident A exhibited intermittent confusion and occasional agitation. Today, they appeared restless and wandered multiple times during the night, making it difficult to ensure they rested well. Notably, they reported a mild but persistent pain in their lower back, which we will monitor closely.

Resident B struggled with increased apathy and showed signs of nausea throughout the day. Their appetite was noticeably reduced, and they only consumed half of their meal at lunch. Despite encouragement, their intake of fluids was minimal, necessitating a hydration plan review.

Resident C experienced significant discomfort with itching and redness on their legs, which was addressed with topical treatment. They displayed episodes of breathlessness, particularly when transferring from the bed to a wheelchair. We have documented their pain levels for a detailed review by the palliative care team.

Resident D needed complete assistance with daily hygiene, as they are unable to manage any self-care activities. Their nails were trimmed today due to excessive length. Although they received visitors in the morning, they remained disoriented and required constant reminders of their surroundings. They reported occasional shortness of breath, particularly after light exertion.

Resident E appeared increasingly restless at night, often becoming agitated and requiring redirection to their room. They had difficulty eating, despite encouragement, and their meals were left mostly uneaten. Concerns were raised over their noticeable weight loss. Additionally, they mentioned experiencing pain in their joints, which seemed to affect their mobility and transfer efforts.

Resident A was observed having difficulty breathing and experiencing significant back pain this morning. She remained in her wheelchair most of the day due to these discomforts and required full assistance to transfer to her bed. Despite efforts to alleviate her pain with medication, she continues to exhibit signs of distress. Her family has requested a care plan review.

Resident B did not eat much at breakfast or lunch, showing a noticeable decrease in appetite. She required encouragement and assistance with eating but still left most of her food untouched. She also appeared apathic and disoriented, unable to engage much with staff or fellow residents. Later in the day, she reported feeling nauseous and experienced loose stools.

Resident C showed signs of restlessness and was wandering around the hallways during the night. He frequently called out for help and seemed confused about his surroundings. The night staff reported that he had difficulty sleeping and needed assistance to reposition in bed several times. He also complained of tightness in his chest and minor pain that seemed to limit his mobility.

Resident D has developed redness and itching on her lower legs, and the skin around these areas looks fragile. Although she is mostly bedridden, this morning she struggled with significant discomfort, making it hard to find a comfortable position. Additionally, her nails appeared untrimmed, and there’s a notable increase in her agitation and irritability.

Resident E appears to be experiencing severe chronic pain and has been vocal about her distress throughout the day. She did not respond well to her usual pain management routine, requiring additional intervention. There is also a growing oedema on her left arm that needs further assessment. Despite several attempts to engage her in light activities, she remained largely unresponsive and withdrawn.
